Museum technical data supplies the 1998-cc engine, rear mid position, rear drive and aluminium chassis. cars.specification_market: Original second-generation production R26.R announced in 2008; Renault’s German release is dated April 2009 but retains the October 2008 introduction statement. Explicit 169 kW / 230 PS, 310 Nm, six-speed and front drive are used. Optional titanium exhaust, roll cage and Toyo R888 are not standardised. Unqualified vehicle mass is omitted. A separate July 2008 manufacturer release corroborates the launch and historical significance. Photograph identifies a 2009 example, not proof of installed options.
cars.summary: The R26.R established a focused Renault Sport road-hatch formula through extensive weight reduction, a limited-slip front axle and track-developed suspension, setting a contemporary Nurburgring benchmark for its category.

cars.generation: Original rear-engine Berlinette 1600 S road series
cars.specification_market: Original 1565-cc 1600 S road car, Renault Classic history pages 14–15 and version table page 34. The table dates the version to 1969, while the narrative labels its arrival under the 1970 catalogue; the reference uses 1970 without claiming a separate year variant. Its native 122 CH DIN is retained, not replaced with common 125-PS or competition 155/165-plus figures. Group 4 1596/1796-cc and later 1605-cc SC/SI are excluded. No racing gearbox or mass is inferred. Photo identifies a 1971 1600 S exterior with auxiliary lamps; engine, modifications and factory configuration are unverified.
cars.summary: The original A110 Berlinette is central to Alpine’s rally identity: the family won the inaugural 1973 World Rally Championship for manufacturers, while its road cars embodied the same compact, lightweight sports-car philosophy.
